name: AI21 Labs
funding_before_failure: $300M Series D (May 2025) reported; Calcalist says it never closed. Last confirmed: 2023 Series C ($1.4B valuation)
what_happened: Headcount cut from ~180 to ~70; dropped standalone models for Maestro agent platform
precise_reason: Acquisition talks with Nebius ended; standalone models not a sustainable revenue stream
lesson: Don't compete head-on with frontier labs; an announced round is not a closed round

name: Hailo
what_happened: ~10% cut in Jan; ~110 of 220 staff left in Jun; acquired by Microchip (closed Sep 21)
precise_reason: Funding pressure; valuation reportedly halved to <$500M; SPAC stalled
lesson: Hardware needs a financing plan B; a SPAC is not a plan

name: Orbex
funding_before_failure: GBP 138.5M total; Series D failed in 2025
precise_reason: Fundraising and M&A failed; takeover collapsed; losing ~GBP 2M/month
lesson: Capital-intensive deep tech dies when the bridge round fails

name: Parker
lesson: Debt-financed lending plus a hoped-for exit is fragile

name: Tally (DAO governance)
precise_reason: No venture-scale business in governance tooling; looser US crypto rules cut demand
lesson: Regulation-driven demand can vanish; check market size

name: Character.AI
what_happened: Chapter 11; Disney $20M stalking-horse bid for IP licence
precise_reason: Legal, regulatory and operational headwinds incl. teen-safety lawsuits
lesson: Trust and safety is existential in consumer AI

name: ClimateAi
lesson: Climate-software budgets are cyclical

name: Monarch Tractor
precise_reason: Dealer lawsuits over under-performing tractors; failed software pivot
lesson: Hardware must work before you scale sales

name: Twiga Foods
precise_reason: Years of financial pressure; failed restructuring; capital-heavy economics
lesson: Logistics marketplaces need positive contribution margin early

name: Pulley
what_happened: Shutdown; service ends Dec 8; Carta takes customers
lesson: Being the challenger in a winner-take-most category is risky

name: Front
lesson: AI agents pressure support-software seats

name: Robin AI
what_happened: Managed services sold; Microsoft hired engineers
precise_reason: GBP 12M losses on GBP 8M revenue; services-heavy model
lesson: Human-in-the-loop margins kill the AI-software multiple

name: Yupp
precise_reason: Weak product-market fit; labs moved to paid expert data
lesson: Frontier-model progress can erase your market

name: Ollie
precise_reason: Competition from Meta products; could not raise more
lesson: Privacy alone is not a moat against Big Tech

name: Huxe
what_happened: Shut down a day after Spotify shipped a similar feature
lesson: A feature of a big platform is not a company

name: Klump
precise_reason: Slow bank integrations; debt raise never came
lesson: Lending startups need committed debt lines

name: Pendo
lesson: Mature SaaS re-tooling for AI

name: ClickUp
lesson: Mature SaaS re-tooling for AI

name: SuperOps
funding_before_failure: Series C-stage per Tracxn (~$54.4M over 4 rounds; verify)
lesson: AI is reshaping engineering headcount even at funded SaaS

name: GoKwik
lesson: Plan headcount around AI automation

name: Covrzy
lesson: Keep 18+ months of runway

name: VentureCrowd
what_happened: Parent entered administration; creditors seeking A$7.3M
lesson: Platform businesses need sustained deal volume

name: Centrical
what_happened: Narrowed customer base and cut headcount, then raised
lesson: Focus before raising can unlock capital
